title: Splitting a nondegenerate quadratic completed local algebra after degree at most two
statement:
Let $F$ be a field and $S$ a finitely generated commutative $F$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Let $\varepsilon:S\to F$ be an $F$-algebra homomorphism [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient], let $\mathfrak p=\ker\varepsilon$, and put $A=S_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Let $a,b,c\in F$ satisfy $\Delta=b^2-4ac\ne0$, and write $q=au^2+buv+cv^2\in F[[u,v]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Suppose given an $F$-algebra isomorphism $\widehat A\cong F[[u,v]]/(q)$, where completion is at the maximal ideal [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] and the $F$-action on $\widehat A$ is induced by $F\to S\to A\to\widehat A$. There exists a finite separable field extension $K/F$ [def-pc-field-extension] [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension] with $[K:F]\le2$ such that the following holds. Form the algebra tensor product $S_K=S\otimes_FK$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], the $K$-algebra map $\varepsilon_K:S_K\to K$, $s\otimes\lambda\mapsto\varepsilon(s)\lambda$, its maximal kernel $\mathfrak q$, and the local ring $B=(S_K)_{\mathfrak q}$. The structural map $K\to B/\mathfrak qB$ is an isomorphism and there are $K$-algebra isomorphisms
$$\widehat B\cong K[[u,v]]/(au^2+buv+cv^2)\cong K[[U,V]]/(UV).$$
Here coefficients in the middle ring are transported through the given embedding $F\hookrightarrow K$; the second isomorphism is induced by an invertible $K$-linear change of the two power-series variables.

source.place: Tags 0CBT (remark-quadratic-extension) and 0CBU (remark-trivial-quadratic-extension), quadratic splitting and split completed equation; Varieties Tag 0C54 (varieties.tex, lemma-base-change-complete-local-ring), completed presentation after field extension. This is the explicit affine quadratic argument of the returned item, steps 6-8, before the final field-tower assembly.

proof.text: The map $\varepsilon$ is onto, since it fixes $F$, and induces $S/\mathfrak p\cong F$. Hence $\mathfrak p$ is maximal and $A/\mathfrak pA\cong F$. Apply [lem-trf-separable-evaluation-local-base-change] with base field $F$, residue extension $F/F$, and extension field $F$ to see that $A$ is Noetherian local. Put $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak pA$; it is finitely generated. By [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal], $\widehat A/\mathfrak m\widehat A\cong F$ through the given coefficient map. An element of $\widehat A$ with nonzero residue is a unit: its coordinates in every $A/\mathfrak m^j$ are units, and their inverses are compatible, giving its inverse in the inverse limit. Thus $\mathfrak m\widehat A$ is its unique maximal ideal. The given $F$-algebra isomorphism with $F[[u,v]]/(q)$ preserves the unique maximal ideals and all their powers; it and its inverse are consequently continuous. The variable ideal of the quotient is its unique maximal ideal, since a series with nonzero constant coefficient has a formal geometric-series inverse.

proof.text: In the no-root case set $K=F[T]/(p)$ and $r=\overline T$. By [lem-trf-irreducible-polynomial-quotient-field], $K$ is a field. The power basis in [lem-weil-pbc-monic-quotient-free] is $1,r$, so $[K:F]=2$ and every element is $x+yr$, $x,y\in F$. Hence $K=F(r)$. Evaluation at $r$ is the quotient map (a polynomial evaluates to its own class), so its kernel is $(p)$; the monic minimal polynomial of $r$ is therefore $p$. Step 2 makes $r$ separable, and [lem-trf-simple-separable-field-extension] gives separability of $K/F$. In the root case or the case $a=0$, $K=F$ has degree one and is separable, since every element $x\in F$ has minimal polynomial $T-x$ with derivative $1$. Thus all cases give a finite separable $K/F$ of degree at most two.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-separable-evaluation-local-base-change] now with base field $F$, residue extension $F/F$, and the constructed $K$. Its evaluation map is exactly $\varepsilon_K$, so its maximal kernel is the stated $\mathfrak q$ and its localization is $B$. It gives $B/\mathfrak qB\cong K$ by evaluation; the inverse is the structural map, since evaluation fixes $K$. The coefficient map $F\to\widehat A$ is a section of the residue map by step 1. Invert the given isomorphism to obtain the continuous presentation $F[[u,v]]\twoheadrightarrow\widehat A$ with kernel $(q)\subseteq(u,v)$. Therefore [lem-trf-field-extension-completion-presentation], with $n=2$ and the single relation $q$, gives the required $K$-algebra isomorphism $\widehat B\cong K[[u,v]]/(q)$, with all coefficients extended by $F\hookrightarrow K$.

source.place: Tags 0C4Y and 0C50 at the evaluation point; Tag 0C54, lemma-base-change-complete-local-ring, extension of the specified presentation.

proof.text: The field case of [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-field-cohen-regular-complete] makes $K[[u,v]]$ and $K[[U,V]]$ complete for their variable ideals. Since $L_1,L_2\in(u,v)$, [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-universal-property-complete] defines a $K$-algebra map $\phi:K[[U,V]]\to K[[u,v]]$, $(U,V)^{\mathsf T}\mapsto M(u,v)^{\mathsf T}$. The same statement applied to $M^{-1}(U,V)^{\mathsf T}$ defines $\psi$ in the other direction. The two composites fix every constant and variable by $MM^{-1}=M^{-1}M=1$; uniqueness in that universal property makes both composites the identity. Thus the invertible linear change extends to an isomorphism of the power-series rings.

source.place: Tag 0CBU, remark-trivial-quadratic-extension, (1),(2),(5); formal substitution uses algebra.tex Tag 032C and the universal-property passage of more-algebra.tex Tag 07NL.

proof.text: We have $\phi(UV)=L_1L_2=q$ and $\psi(q)=UV$. Consequently the maps send the two principal ideals onto one another and descend to inverse $K$-algebra maps $K[[U,V]]/(UV)\cong K[[u,v]]/(q)$: the map on a quotient class is the class of its image, and the composites are identities because they were identities before quotienting. Invert this isomorphism and compose with step 5 to obtain both isomorphisms asserted in the statement. The second is induced by the specified invertible linear change.
